questions.question: What happens without engine oil?

options.text: A vehicle will get better gas mileage.
An engine can be destroyed quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: An engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is essential. Without it, an engine can be destroyed very quickly.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: Newer vehicles have a yellow diamond-shaped knob for the parking brake. Pull it out to set the brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: What do the two markings on a front brake limiting valve usually say?
questions.explanation: Some older air brake systems made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings.

questions.question: Is it legal to send text messages while driving?

options.text: Yes, if the messages are short.
Yes, if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is illegal.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: You are not permitted to stop and exit the vehicle.
You are encouraged not to exit the vehicle.
You are allowed to exit only if the vehicle is in reverse.
You are allowed to exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are allowed to exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting. You can check the vehicle's position no more than twice. During straight line backing, you can look only once.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with the belts?

options.text: Leave them alone and do not inspect them.
Inspect them only about once a month.

questions.explanation: Check all belts for tightness and wear during your pre-trip inspection.

questions.question: How do you complete an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Pull forward to the right, then back in a straight line.
Pull forward to the left, then back in a straight line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the left. The vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep
When you want to take a nap
The time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back the debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: What can a hand valve do?

options.text: Keep a truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve can be used to keep a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver gradually apply spring brakes. A lever on the dashboard controls it in equipped vehicles.

questions.question: What happens when you overload a vehicle with cargo?

options.text: It usually has no effect on the vehicle.
It can make steering and braking harder to control.
It can damage the electrical system.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make steering and braking harder to control.
questions.explanation: Too much cargo can affect how your vehicle steers, brakes, and maintains speed. Learn to tell when cargo is overloaded or not balanced properly.

questions.question: In an emergency stop, what should you do?

options.text: Lock the wheels and slide to a stop.
Keep your vehicle going straight while you stop.
Turn your vehicle while you stop.
Expect your vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle going straight while you stop.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle traveling straight. This lets you still turn if you need to.

questions.question: While driving, what should you do?

options.text: Plan how to escape any dangerous situation that might happen.
Only focus on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to escape any dangerous situation that might happen.
questions.explanation: Check the road ahead for hazards while you drive. Have a plan ready for any dangers that could occur.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, what should you check the hoses for?

options.text: Whether they are connected to the battery.
Whether they have the right amount of flexibility.

questions.explanation: When checking a power steering system, inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look specifically for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Explosives are classified as Class 1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a rear-end crash and makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up only makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Do not check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: When turning quickly to avoid a hazard, keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times. A firm grip gives you the control you need to turn quickly.

questions.question: How do you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Use the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights and let drivers behind you know you are slowing down. Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you get?
questions.explanation: To operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must get a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When asked to turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.explanation: When turning during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Manual air tank drains should be:

options.text: Opened to drain the tanks after each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opened to drain the tanks after each day.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in brake systems collects water and oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up. You must open manual air tank drains every day to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, a driver can increase visibility by:

options.text: Flashing their lights on and off.

questions.explanation: When driving at dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to make your vehicle more visible.

questions.question: What should you do when an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Try to stay in the other driver's way.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not speed up to challenge them. Do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Is not available for most trucks.
Is not helpful in most situations.

questions.explanation: Starting between 1997 and 1999, most commercial trucks, trailers, and dollies must have ABS.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch in the grooves

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Do not mix tire sizes.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should:

options.text: Pull over and find out what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and find out what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, stop driving right away and check for problems. Your engine could fail or catch fire.

questions.question: The emergency brake system uses:

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three braking systems: a service brake system, a parking brake system, and an emergency brake system. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: When driving in winter, which of the following needs extra attention during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: When driving in winter, make sure the coolant and antifreeze are at safe levels.

questions.question: If involved in an accident, which of the following is not recommended?

options.text: Trying to move your vehicle to the side of the road

questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, and collect information. Do not leave the scene. You can lose your license for leaving an accident.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Do this even during the daytime.

questions.question: When should you use your mirrors?

options.text: Only when there may be an emergency.
Have a helper watch your blind spots instead.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently while driving. Look at both side mirrors regularly.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which of these should be fixed?

options.text: A broken exhaust pipe, muffler, or tailpipe

questions.explanation: Exhaust system problems are serious. Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin if the system is damaged. Check for loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, brackets, clamps, or bolts. Also check that exhaust parts are not rubbing against fuel lines or tires, and that no parts are leaking.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is broken?

options.text: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your brakes still work.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's brakes will still work without ABS. Drive and brake as you normally would. Get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration good or bad?

options.text: It is okay at slow speeds.
It is okay at all speeds.
It is bad at all speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is bad at all speeds.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Do not jerk the vehicle. Rough acceleration can damage the engine.

questions.question: For a vehicle with air brakes, what condition should the air compressor belt be in?
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor belt before each drive. The belt should be tight and in good condition.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, they are okay for rear tires.
Yes, they are okay when carrying heavy loads.

questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been welded. They are not safe.

questions.question: Why are multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions used?

options.text: To make the vehicle run more smoothly

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears for vehicles.

questions.question: If you need to turn to avoid a hazard, should you brake?

options.text: No, do not brake. It may lock the wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, do not brake. It may lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while making a quick turn. Braking could lock your wheels and cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When backing a truck, which mirrors should you use?

options.text: No mirrors. Do not use a helper.

questions.explanation: Always use both side mirrors when backing. Have someone help you if possible.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects muscle control, reaction time, vision, and judgment. Some people show signs of impairment after just one drink. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What can happen with improperly loaded cargo?

options.text: It looks bad to other drivers.
It can hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
It makes the vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can hurt or kill the driver during a sudden stop.
questions.explanation: Loose cargo is dangerous. During a sudden stop, unsecured cargo can fall and injure or kill the driver.

questions.question: When driving in wet conditions, what does a lack of spray from other vehicles' tires mean?

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is caught under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, no spray from tires means ice has formed on the road. Drive with extra caution in freezing, wet weather.

questions.question: How should you accelerate on a wet road with poor traction?

options.text: Do not worry about the pavement.

questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly when driving on surfaces with poor traction, like wet roads.

questions.question: What happens if you have more than one driver's license?

options.text: You probably will not get caught.
You are not doing anything wrong.
There is no way authorities will find out.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver's license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and fines up to $5,000.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic past.

questions.explanation: When stopped on the road shoulder, place emergency warning devices, like reflective triangles, within 10 minutes.

questions.question: What are tie-downs used for?
questions.explanation: Tie-downs secure cargo on flatbed trailers and in vans to stop it from shifting or falling. Shifting cargo can affect how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: What can cause hydraulic brakes to fail?
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes usually fail because of lost hydraulic pressure. Brakes can also fade from overuse on long downhill drives.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a header board, what should it be?

options.text: Light up when the engine starts.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check that the header board is secure, undamaged, and strong enough to contain cargo.

questions.question: When you start the engine during a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for unusual noises.
